scenes.title: Where and when
narration: Danza Prima is an ancient dance from Asturias, Spain, with possible Celtic linguistic roots and martial-religious origins.
It has been preserved as a communal circle dance accompanied by heroic ballads and the Celtic bagpipe.
Historically, dancers used sticks resembling battle maces, suggesting a connection to warrior rituals.

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: Danza Prima is a communal dance that brings together all members of the community, from the elderly to the young.
Its martial and possibly religious origins suggest it was performed during significant local events or festivals, possibly linked to historical remembrance or rites of passage.
The dance symbolizes unity, heritage, and the continuity of tradition across generations.
Today it is a living tradition.

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: Danza Prima is danced in a circle moving from left to right.
Dancers step forward first with the right foot, then retreat two steps, creating a slow, pendulum-like motion.
The body and arms swing in time with the steps, and dancers may carry sticks, which they move rhythmically.
Watch for Pendulum Step, Stick Swing.

scenes.title: The people
narration: Danza Prima is preserved mainly in Asturias but similar stick dances and circle dances exist in northern Spain and Galicia, where they are known by different names such as 'muñeira'.
Danza Prima likely descends from ancient Celtic and Roman influences in northern Spain, combining martial, religious, and communal elements into a folk dance form.
